builders.text:
Most good organizations when faced with an existential crisis that doesn’t destroy them will return meaner and out for blood.

They have seen what failure could look like and are ready to go to war to make sure that never happens.

I felt this over and over again at Meta. 

Nvidia isn’t going to hold back now.
builders.textZh:
大多数优秀的组织在面临一场不会摧毁它们的生存危机时，都会变得更加卑鄙和流血。

他们已经看到了失败可能是什么样子，并准备好发动战争以确保这种情况永远不会发生。

我在 Meta 一次又一次地感受到了这一点。 

英伟达现在不会再犹豫了。

builders.name: Madhu Guru
builders.bio: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
builders.text:
Part of the disconnect is that the name “data” massively undersells what it truly represents in model development.

People who are not close to model development think of data as this  inert commodity you buy and shovel into a model, like coal.

In reality great data encodes incredibly high value knowledge, taste and expertise, often articulated and structured in ways that did not exist previously. 

This makes it one of THE fundamental building blocks for creating increasingly capable intelligence across domains. 

Data will continue to be incredibly central to the intelligence industry .
builders.textZh:
部分脱节在于“数据”这个名字大大低估了它在模型开发中真正代表的含义。

不熟悉模型开发的人认为数据是您购买并铲入模型中的惰性商品，就像煤炭一样。

事实上，大数据编码了令人难以置信的高价值知识、品味和专业知识，通常以以前不存在的方式表达和结构化。 

这使其成为跨领域创建能力日益增强的智能的基本构建模块之一。 

数据将继续成为情报行业的核心。

builders.bio: General Partner @SPC, Co-Founder @Bevel_Health | Ex: Early Eng @facebook, CTO @Dropbox, Board @Flipkart | Optimist, Builder, Dad
builders.text:
Sometimes you need to travel abroad to deeply appreciate just how inspirational America is to the rest of the world.

Countries and individuals aspire to have an entreprenurial ecosystem like ours. A capital market base like ours.

They don't want to be like China or the UK or Denmark. 

They want to be like America.

And this is particularly true for the most ambitious people in every country. They are students of how America builds.

This doesn't mean we cannot do better ourselves. We must and we will.
builders.textZh:
有时你需要出国旅行才能深刻体会美国对世界其他地方的鼓舞人心。

各国和个人都渴望拥有像我们这样的创业生态系统。像我们这样的资本市场基础。

他们不想像中国、英国或丹麦那样。 

他们想像美国一样。

对于每个国家最雄心勃勃的人来说尤其如此。他们是美国如何建设的学生。

这并不意味着我们不能做得更好。我们必须而且将会这样做。

builders.name: Amjad Masad
builders.bio: ceo @replit. civilizationist
builders.text:
Great meeting with VP @JDVance on Friday to discuss American AI leadership, cybersecurity, and modernizing our nation’s software infrastructure.

We also discussed an issue close to my heart: American leadership in open-weight AI. 

Our allies want sovereign AI and are increasingly looking to Chinese open models. At home, American startups need a competitive model ecosystem.

America could win the frontier AI race and still lose the global AI ecosystem.

Very happy to see Jensen back at Nvidia. He’s been one of the most important champions of American open-weight AI.
builders.textZh:
周五与副总裁 @JDVance 进行了精彩的会面，讨论了美国人工智能的领导地位、网络安全以及我国软件基础设施的现代化。

我们还讨论了一个我很关心的问题：美国在开放式人工智能领域的领导地位。 

我们的盟友想要主权人工智能，并且越来越多地寻求中国的开放模式。在国内，美国初创企业需要一个有竞争力的模式生态系统。

美国可能会赢得前沿人工智能竞赛，但仍然会失去全球人工智能生态系统。

很高兴看到 Jensen 回到 Nvidia。他是美国公开重量级人工智能最重要的拥护者之一。

builders.bio: ceo @replit. civilizationist
builders.text:
New research from Replit on scaling laws for agent swarms. 

We show that scaling the number of agents can yield dramatic performance gains, but unlike traditional scaling laws, more compute doesn't necessarily translate into better results, and how agents organize themselves matters.

- Given a fixed two-hour window, Opus 5.5 went from a 3.7x speedup on NumPy with one agent to 18.9x with 32 agents.

- GPT-6.2 Astra was the strongest solo agent but exhibited negative scaling beyond 8 agents.

- Models spontaneously developed different organizational structures. Decentralized swarms scaled bett
builders.textZh:
Replit 关于代理群缩放定律的新研究。 

我们表明，扩展代理的数量可以带来显着的性能提升，但与传统的扩展法则不同，更多的计算并不一定会转化为更好的结果，代理如何组织自己很重要。

- 给定固定的两小时窗口，Opus 5.5 在使用 1 个智能体的 NumPy 上的加速速度从 3.7 倍提高到使用 32 个智能体的 18.9 倍。

- GPT-6.2 Astra 是最强的单独代理，但在超过 8 个代理时表现出负扩展。

- 模型自发地发展出不同的组织结构。去中心化集群规模贝特

builders.bio: Builder.  Harvard’17. Instagram: https://t.co/aJqTEMrL2L YouTube: https://t.co/8xzbGWtf6w GitHub: https://t.co/KCuEajezlL
builders.text:
You can post on social media every day and still be a very private person; the two are not contradictory 

Many people have the misconception that sharing your thoughts online means turning your whole life into an open book for others to see. This can’t be further from the truth

I post almost every day but I only share a tiny sliver of my life & thoughts, probably less than 1%. I only share what I’m comfortable with sharing

The key is to find out which 1% is at the intersection of “interesting to others” and “comfortable for you”
builders.textZh:
你可以每天在社交媒体上发帖，但仍然是一个非常注重隐私的人；两者并不矛盾 

许多人有一种误解，认为在网上分享你的想法意味着把你的整个生活变成一本打开的书供别人查看。这与事实相差甚远

我几乎每天都会发帖，但我只分享我生活和想法的一小部分，可能不到 1%。我只分享我愿意分享的内容

关键是要找出哪1%处于“别人感兴趣”和“你觉得舒服”的交叉点
